sections.headline: Aaron Rai's 65 in Round 4 seals a three-shot PGA Championship victory at -9, closing with four straight rounds of 70 or better.
sections.leaders: Rai dominates at -9, finishing 3 shots clear of Smalley and Rahm at -6. His winning formula: +1.32 SG approach, +0.67 SG off-the-tee, and +3.93 SG putting—textbook ball-striking and clutch greens. Thomas lurks at -5 with identical total SG to Rai (+5.61), but couldn't match the leader's closing 65.

on_fire.name: Kurt Kitayama
on_fire.blurb: Finished T10 at -3 with the tour's best SG day: +7.61 total, anchored by +5.23 SG putting. His R4 63 was the lowest round of the week, showcasing elite putter form when it mattered most.

on_fire.name: Matt Fitzpatrick
on_fire.blurb: T14 at -2 but second in cumulative SG (+5.61) thanks to +3.98 SG putting and steady +0.80 approach play. Closed with a 65 to claw back into contention on a brutal setup.

on_fire.name: Justin Thomas
on_fire.blurb: Matched Rai's R4 65 to reach -5 and T4, posting +5.61 total SG led by +1.47 SG approach and +3.81 SG putting. His ball-striking was the best among chasers.

to_watch.name: Alex Smalley
to_watch.blurb: Tied second at -6 after a steady 70 in Round 4. At T2, just 3 back with a legitimate path had Sunday been extended—stayed competitive throughout but couldn't generate the birdie flurries Rai found.

to_watch.name: Jon Rahm
to_watch.blurb: Co-runner-up at -6 with a 68 in Round 4. His consistency (70-67-68 arc in final three rounds) kept him in the window, but lacked the red-hot putting that separated Rai and Kitayama.

sections.your_picks: Your core trio—Thomas (T4, -5), McIlroy (T7, -4), and Schauffele (T7, -4)—all finished in the top 10 and combined for +5.61, +2.61, and +2.61 SG respectively. Thomas and Schauffele have course pedigree (both with prior victories), but none caught Rai's closing surge; Fitzpatrick at T14 (-2) was your biggest SG generator at +5.61 total.
sections.round_story: Scoring tightened dramatically: the field shot -4.5 average in R4 compared to R3's -3.1. Rai's 67-65 back-to-back sealed it; the chasing pack stayed bunched, with six players at -4 or -5 but unable to bridge a 3-shot gap forged by superior putting (+3.93 vs. field avg +1.2) and approach play in the final 36 holes.
